page: Amazon Web Services r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance profiles across multiple domains. In CPU-centric evaluations, the r7a.8xlarge achieves top 25% results in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a strong PassMark CPU score of 62,261.4. Memory performance is highlighted by a top 25% read-only small block memory bandwidth of 4,741.49 GB/sec and a strong write bandwidth of 105.97 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block read-only bandwidth falls into the middle 50% tier. For specialized workloads, the instance demonstrates top 10% performance in prompt processing for small language models, processing 4,611.49 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.8xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads due to its DDR5 memory architecture and dedicated physical cores. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents a tradeoff, as all storage operations must traverse the network, potentially impacting I/O-heavy workloads. The absence of a GPU also limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training, though it remains efficient for smaller-scale CPU-based inference.

This instance configuration is suited for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, where it achieves strong PassMark database scores and 78.07 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It is also appropriate for software compilation, text processing, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
